newsitem.title: UK: Brent Walker examines William Hill options.
newsitem.headline: Brent Walker examines William Hill options.

text.p: Debt-laden UK leisure company Brent Walker Group Plc is reviewing the position of bookmaker William Hill, its last major asset, the company said on Thursday.

Brent Walker noted that its lending arrangements terminate at the end of the year and that steps will have to be taken to realise the value of the asset by that date. If it decides to retain it, an agreement will be required from the banks to extend the current facilities.
Chairman Sir Brian Goswell said that the group's bank borrowings exceed 1.3 billion stg. The deficit on shareholders' funds amounts to 1.03 billion.
William Hill, a chain of some 1,700 shops, is valued at some 500 million stg, so a sale would not cover what it owes to the banks in loans and overdrafts.
Turnover from the company's betting services increased by 6.2 percent in 1996, while profits climbed 30 percent to 50.3 million stg.
Goswell said that trading since the beginning of the year had been encouraging but noted that the betting services industry was a volatile one.
But it added that the introduction of "fruit machines" and numbers betting to shops had made a significant new contribution to the business.

Profit before interest and tax totalled 216.5 million stg in 1996, helped by a gain on the sale of the Pubmaster chain and a payment from Grand Metropolitan Plc relating to the settlement of a long-running dispute over the purchase price of William Hill in 1989.
Options open to Brent Walker on William Hill include flotation, merger, a trade sale, or the reversal of the chain into a Brent Walker shell.
Bass Plc, which has 930 UK betting shops in its Coral chain, has been tipped as a possible bidder.
